quick.summary: How to know when a task is actually finished and ready to use.
quick.takeaway: Write down how you will test the work before you start building.

beats.line: My team built the new search box. But it searches nothing.
They said it was ready. How is that done?
Imagine ordering a baked potato. The chef hands you a cold, raw potato.
It is a potato. But you cannot eat it yet.
Your work needs to state what makes it truly usable.
We call these conditions acceptance criteria.
Can I just say how to test it?
Exactly. Write the test on the card before work starts.
So, a search box must actually return a result to be finished.
Now you are serving a beautifully cooked potato.

quiz.question: How do you ensure a feature is actually usable when done?
options: Define how to test it before starting.
Let the developers decide at the end.
Ask the users after it launches.
Only build the easiest parts first.
quiz.explanation: Writing the test criteria up front ensures the team knows exactly what a finished, usable feature looks like.

quiz.question: Acceptance criteria are best written after the work is finished.
quiz.explanation: They must be written before work begins so the team knows what goal to aim for.
